title: uat-scheduling cancel/reassign/assign/manual authenticate but never authorize and never check group ownership
actor: Customer B (CUST-ATTACKER-B). REAL non-preview platform session cookie issued by lib/platform-session.ts issuePlatformSession over a verified customer_otp identity binding (principalKey customer:CUST-ATTACKER-B). resolveActor() returned {roleCode:'customer', permissions:['pricing.view','scheduling.book'], developmentPreview:false, identitySource:'customer_otp'} - verified by calling resolveActor directly in the probe. B owns no binding to CUST-VICTIM-A and holds neither customers.manage nor bookings.manage.
request: POST https://uat.pawspace.in/api/uat-scheduling (app/api/uat-scheduling/route.ts POST), cookie = B's platform session. Four payloads against victim group GRP-VICTIM-001 created by customer A: {action:'reassign',groupId:'GRP-VICTIM-001',customerId:'CUST-ATTACKER-B',reason:'attacker reassign',...}; {action:'manual',providerId:'groom_p2',reason:'attacker manual override',...}; {action:'assign',providerId:'groom_p2',reason:'attacker assign',...}; {action:'cancel',reason:'attacker cancel',...}.
response: reassign 200 {"data":{"groupId":"GRP-VICTIM-001","status":"assigned","provider":{"id":"groom_p2",...},"previousProviderId":"groom_p1","shortlist":[...],"explanation":...}}; manual 200 (same shape); assign 200 (same shape); cancel 200 {"data":{"groupId":"GRP-VICTIM-001","status":"cancelled"}}. Every response claims success and returns the victim's provider roster, shortlist and scoring explanation to the attacker. The only 409 seen was 'Select one of the three recommended providers or use Manual assignment' when assign named a provider outside the stored shortlist - a business-shape check, not an authorization check; assign with a shortlisted provider returned 200.
d1_before: scheduling_assignment_decisions: {group_id:'GRP-VICTIM-001', selected_provider_id:'groom_p1', status:'assigned', actor_id:'system', reason:'Auto-assigned by ranked rules'}. scheduling_reservations: [{id:'GRP-VICTIM-001_groom_p1_1_...', customer_id:'CUST-VICTIM-A', provider_id:'groom_p1', status:'assigned'}].
d1_after: scheduling_assignment_decisions: {group_id:'GRP-VICTIM-001', selected_provider_id:'groom_p2', status:'cancelled', actor_id:'customer:CUST-ATTACKER-B', reason:'attacker cancel'}. scheduling_reservations: all rows for the group status='cancelled', every row still carrying customer_id='CUST-VICTIM-A' while provider_id was rewritten groom_p1 -> groom_p2. security_audit_events recorded scheduling.reassign / scheduling.manual / scheduling.assign / scheduling.cancel on resource GRP-VICTIM-001 with actor_email='customer:CUST-ATTACKER-B' and outcome='completed' - the platform's own audit trail records the cross-tenant writes as authorized.
canonical_failure: POST /api/uat-scheduling with action in {cancel,reassign,assign,manual} routes straight to operateAssignment() after resolveActor() alone - no requirePermission, no requireCustomerOwnership, and no comparison of the actor to the scheduling group's customer_id - so any authenticated customer holding only ['pricing.view','scheduling.book'] can reassign, manually override, or cancel any other customer's scheduling group by group id and receive HTTP 200 plus that group's provider shortlist.
blast_radius: Every scheduling group in the platform is writable by group id from any logged-in customer session. An attacker can cancel a stranger's confirmed grooming/boarding job, move it onto a provider of their choosing (creating commission offers on that provider), free the victim's held capacity for themselves, and read the victim's ranked provider shortlist and scoring rationale. The victim's reservation rows keep the victim's customer_id, so the group looks legitimately owned while its provider and status are attacker-controlled, and the audit log attributes the change to a 'completed' action rather than a denial.

title: Any customer can rebind another customer's app install to themselves through the public OTP verify endpoint, erasing the victim from acquisition attribution and from the App-Inbound lead sweep
risk_category: authorization / cross-tenant identity rebinding via unauthenticated public endpoint
actor: Attacker B - an anonymous member of the public. POST /api/customer-otp carries NO authentication of any kind (no session cookie, no forwarded identity, no resolveActor call anywhere in app/api/customer-otp/route.ts); the only gate is sameOriginWrite(), which is satisfied by omitting the Origin header. B proves only its OWN phone (9000000002 / 9000000004) via its own sandbox OTP; installId is an unvalidated attacker-supplied string in the same body.
request: Public endpoint app/api/customer-otp/route.ts POST. Step 1 (victim, normal use): {action:'request',phone:'9000000001'} then {action:'verify',challengeId,code:<sandboxCode>,name:'Victim A',installId:'INST-VICTIM-0001'}. Step 2 (attacker, same public endpoint, no auth): {action:'request',phone:'9000000002'} then {action:'verify',challengeId,code:<own sandboxCode>,name:'Attacker B',installId:'INST-VICTIM-0001'} - the victim's install id, replayed verbatim. Route -> verifyCustomerOtp() (lib/customer-otp.ts:72) -> identifyInstall() (lib/app-to-revenue-funnel.ts:47).
response: Attacker's verify returned 200 {"data":{"customerId":"CUS-OTP-08E951FBE0DCFA59E2EB57E8","customerName":"Attacker B","phone":"9000000002","expiresAt":...}} plus a Set-Cookie platform session for B. No warning, no conflict, no 409 - the rebinding is silent and the response claims success.
d1_before: app_installs: {install_id:'INST-VICTIM-0001', source:'google_ads', campaign:'diwali_dogs', os:'android'}. install_identity_links: {install_id:'INST-VICTIM-0001', customer_id:'CUS-OTP-17C2B932CC1AA91924C0B371' (Victim A), identified_at:1787633902949}. lead_work_items after first sweep: [{id:'LWI-...', customer_id:'CUS-OTP-17C2B932CC1AA91924C0B371', source:'App Inbound', status:'active'}].
d1_after: install_identity_links: {install_id:'INST-VICTIM-0001', customer_id:'CUS-OTP-08E951FBE0DCFA59E2EB57E8' (Attacker B), identified_at:1787633902949 - the victim's original identified_at is retained, so the row still looks like the original first identification}. SELECT * FROM install_identity_links returns exactly ONE row for that install: the victim's link is gone, not duplicated. acquisitionFunnelReport() then reports downloads=1, identified=1 where the single identified customer is B - A's google_ads/diwali_dogs acquisition has been transferred to B. Scenario 2 (rebind before the sweep runs, install INST-VICTIM-0002, victim CUS-OTP-62DA8B00F4900CF346103C0E, attacker CUS-OTP-9E7C9948FB8E5DBA630C427D): after the rebind, runAppFunnelSweep reported appInboundLeads:1 and lead_work_items / funnel_producer_marks contain a row for the ATTACKER only - the victim never appears in either table.
canonical_failure: identifyInstall() writes 'INSERT INTO install_identity_links ... ON CONFLICT(install_id) DO UPDATE SET customer_id=excluded.customer_id' with no check that the install is unclaimed and no check that the caller owns the prior claim, and it is reached from the fully public, unauthenticated /api/customer-otp verify action with a caller-supplied installId, so anyone who knows or guesses another customer's install id can point that install at their own customer record with an HTTP 200 and take over its acquisition attribution and its App-Inbound lead.
refutation: Partial scope correction to the frozen wording: a victim who ALREADY has an App-Inbound lead keeps it - funnel_producer_marks is keyed on customer_id, so an existing lead and mark survive the rebind (observed in scenario 1: LEADS_2 contains both the victim's and the attacker's leads). The erasure from the lead sweep is real but prospective: it holds when the rebind lands before the sweep first sees that install (scenario 2, where the victim never got a lead at all). The erasure from acquisition attribution is unconditional and immediate in both scenarios.
blast_radius: Install ids are client-generated device identifiers that travel in app request bodies and logs; one leaked or guessed id is enough. Consequences observed in execution: (1) the install's paid-acquisition source and campaign (google_ads / diwali_dogs, meta_ads / puppy_care) are re-attributed from the real installer to the attacker, corrupting the App Acquisition Funnel report Ops reads; (2) an unbooked victim silently drops out of the App-Inbound Sales sweep and never gets the 10-minute first-call SLA lead, while the attacker gets it; (3) the link row keeps the victim's original identified_at, so the takeover leaves no timestamp trace. Repeated at scale this both starves the sales queue of real leads and lets one actor claim credit for arbitrary installs.

title: Lifecycle idempotency keys are not bound to the booking, stay, session or action: a colliding key silently drops the caller's mutation, returns HTTP 200, and hands back another entity's identifiers
risk_category: cross-tenant data disclosure + silent lost update via unscoped idempotency key
actor: Two DIFFERENT real non-preview providers, each correctly authorized for their OWN booking. WALKER-P1: platform session over a verified partner_otp binding, roleCode 'service_provider', permissions ['bookings.view','scheduling.view','communications.call','communications.message','self_service.view'], owner of BKG-A1 (customer CUST-A). WALKER-P2: identical role and permissions, owner of BKG-B2 (customer CUST-B). Neither holds bookings.manage. requireProviderOwnership passed for each on its own booking - the route's authorization is correct; the leak happens after it.
request: POST /api/walking-lifecycle (app/api/walking-lifecycle/route.ts POST). Call 1, cookie=WALKER-P1: {bookingId:'BKG-A1',action:'accept',idempotencyKey:'IDEM-SHARED-KEY-0001'}. Call 2, cookie=WALKER-P2: {bookingId:'BKG-B2',action:'accept',idempotencyKey:'IDEM-SHARED-KEY-0001'} - a different booking, a different customer, a different provider, the same key. Call 3, cookie=WALKER-P1: {bookingId:'BKG-A1',action:'decline',idempotencyKey:'IDEM-SHARED-KEY-0001',reason:'walker is ill and cannot attend'} - same booking, DIFFERENT action, same key.
response: Call 1: 200 {"data":{"bookingId":"BKG-A1","status":"assigned","providerId":"WALKER-P1"}}. Call 2: 200 {"data":{"bookingId":"BKG-A1","status":"assigned","providerId":"WALKER-P1","duplicatePrevented":true}} - WALKER-P2 asked about BKG-B2 and was handed customer CUST-A's booking id and the rival walker's provider id, with a success status. Call 3: 200 with the same BKG-A1/assigned/WALKER-P1 body - the decline never happened.
d1_after: canonical_bookings: [{id:'BKG-A1',customer_id:'CUST-A',provider_id:'WALKER-P1',status:'assigned'},{id:'BKG-B2',customer_id:'CUST-B',provider_id:'WALKER-P2',status:'confirmed'}] - BKG-B2 was NEVER accepted despite the 200. provider_work_orders: BKG-A1 'accepted', BKG-B2 still 'assigned'. walking_action_keys holds exactly one row {idempotency_key:'IDEM-SHARED-KEY-0001', booking_id:'BKG-A1', action:'accept', result_json:'{"bookingId":"BKG-A1","status":"assigned","providerId":"WALKER-P1"}'} - the booking_id and action columns are recorded but never read back. After call 3, walking_recovery_cases COUNT=0 - the decline produced no recovery case, no ops escalation and no customer notification. security_audit_events logged both as outcome='completed', the second with detail duplicatePrevented:true and resource_id BKG-B2, so the audit trail says the B2 mutation succeeded.
canonical_failure: lib/walking-lifecycle.ts prior() reads 'SELECT result_json FROM walking_action_keys WHERE idempotency_key=?' with no booking_id and no action predicate, and mutateWalkingBooking() consults it BEFORE it loads the booking, so any second caller reusing a key - even a different provider acting for a different customer's booking, or the same provider requesting a different action - gets HTTP 200, has its mutation silently discarded, and receives the first caller's bookingId, status and providerId in the response body.
blast_radius: Cross-tenant identifier disclosure to any authenticated provider who reuses or guesses a key, plus a silent lost update on a real lifecycle transition: a walker's 'decline'/'walker_unavailable' can be swallowed with a 200 so no recovery case opens, no reservation is released and no customer notification is sent, while Ops dashboards and the security audit log both record the action as completed. The identical unscoped-key pattern (SELECT ... WHERE idempotency_key=? only) is present in lib/sitting-lifecycle.ts:20, lib/taxi-lifecycle.ts:25, lib/boarding-stay-lifecycle.ts:41 (keyed per stay) and lib/training-session-lifecycle.ts:23 (keyed per session) - source-level, not separately executed here - so the same collision is reachable across sitting, taxi, boarding stays and training sessions. Client-generated keys such as a schedule group id or a booking id reused across services make accidental collisions likely without an attacker.

title: Idempotency keys in the lead engine do not bind the mutation context: reusing a key on a different lead silently no-ops and returns another lead's record as success
risk_category: unscoped idempotency key - silent lost update plus wrong-record disclosure across leads/customers
actor: Staff operator ops-admin@pawspace.test, non-preview, authenticated by the product's forwarded-identity headers (oai-authenticated-user-email + percent-encoded full name) against a real app_users row with role_code 'founder' and status 'active'. The route gates this action with authorize(request,'customers.manage'), which the founder role satisfies - so the actor is fully authorized for the endpoint; the defect is entirely in the key handling, not the permission check.
request: POST /api/lead-assignment-governance (app/api/lead-assignment-governance/route.ts POST) after seeding an active_uat policy (save_policy 201 + activate_policy 200) and two eligible members. Call 1: {action:'assign',leadId:'LEAD-A',idempotencyKey:'LEAD-IDEM-SHARED-0001',reason:'new_lead'}. Call 2: {action:'assign',leadId:'LEAD-B',idempotencyKey:'LEAD-IDEM-SHARED-0001',reason:'new_lead'} - a different lead belonging to a different CRM contact (CRM-B vs CRM-A). Call 3: {action:'assign',leadId:'LEAD-DOES-NOT-EXIST',idempotencyKey:'LEAD-IDEM-SHARED-0001',reason:'new_lead'}.
response: Call 1: 200 {data:{assignment:{id:'LAS-BA3B5D9A-F4C', lead_id:'LEAD-A', employee_email:'sales1@pawspace.test', status:'current', ...}, duplicatePrevented:false, fallback:false}}. Call 2: 200 with the IDENTICAL assignment object - lead_id:'LEAD-A', employee_email:'sales1@pawspace.test', created_by:'ops-admin@pawspace.test', assigned_at unchanged - plus duplicatePrevented:true. Call 3: 200 with that same LEAD-A assignment object, even though the lead id does not exist at all. All three responses claim success; none is a 404 or 409.
d1_after: lead_assignments holds exactly ONE row: {id:'LAS-BA3B5D9A-F4C', idempotency_key:'LEAD-IDEM-SHARED-0001', lead_id:'LEAD-A', employee_email:'sales1@pawspace.test', status:'current'}. lead_work_items: [{id:'LEAD-A',owner:'sales1@pawspace.test'},{id:'LEAD-B',customer_id:'CRM-B',owner:'Unassigned'}] - LEAD-B was never assigned and still sits unowned. security_audit_events shows three lead.assignment.assign rows, outcome='completed' for all three, with resource_id LEAD-A, LEAD-B and LEAD-DOES-NOT-EXIST but all carrying assignmentId 'LAS-BA3B5D9A-F4C', so the audit trail asserts that LEAD-B and a nonexistent lead were both successfully assigned to LEAD-A's assignment record.
canonical_failure: assignLead() (lib/lead-assignment-governance.ts:42) opens with 'SELECT * FROM lead_assignments WHERE idempotency_key=?' carrying no lead_id predicate and returns that row before leadContext() is ever called, so reusing a key against a different lead - or against a lead id that does not exist - silently discards the assignment and returns the first lead's full assignment row (its lead_id, owner email, team, policy and detail) to the caller as HTTP 200 success.
blast_radius: An unassigned lead is silently starved of an owner while Ops, the API response and the security audit log all report the assignment as completed, so the miss is invisible until the SLA breach. The 200 body discloses another lead's id, its assigned employee's email, team code, policy id and workload detail to whoever made the colliding call. reassignLead() (line 58) opens with the identical unscoped SELECT and additionally supersedes the current assignment before delegating to assignLead, so a colliding key there can leave a lead with its previous assignment superseded. Deterministic keys generated elsewhere in the same module ('outbound-batch:${leadId}', 'rnr-auto-reassign:${leadId}:${owner}') are lead-scoped and therefore safe, but any caller-supplied or campaign/batch-scoped key is not.

title: Customer's own reserve request fabricates the provider roster and overrides Ops-published availability windows
risk_category: privilege escalation - a customer-role write to scheduling roster data that only scheduling.manage should control
actor: Two actors. (1) Ops: ops-scheduler@pawspace.test, non-preview, forwarded-identity headers against an active app_users row with role_code 'founder'; authorize(request,'scheduling.manage') passed. (2) Customer CUST-SELF-01: REAL non-preview platform session over a verified customer_otp binding, roleCode 'customer', permissions ['pricing.view','scheduling.book'] only - it holds NO scheduling.manage and no providers.manage, verified by calling resolveActor directly.
request: Step 1 (Ops, the governed surface): POST /api/provider-capacity-control {action:'set_availability',providerId:'groom_ops',cityId:'maa',zoneId:'chennai-core',date:'2026-09-10',windows:['09:00-10:00']} -> 201, row id 'availability_groom_ops_2026-09-10_chennai-core', source 'operations'. Step 2 (customer, own reserve): POST /api/uat-scheduling {clientRequestId:'GRP-SELF-01',customerId:'CUST-SELF-01',petIds:['PET-S1'],serviceCode:'grooming',cityId:'maa',zoneId:'chennai-core',scheduledStart:'2026-09-10T15:00:00.000Z',scheduledEnd:'2026-09-10T17:00:00.000Z',preferredProviderId:'groom_ops'} - a slot five hours outside what Ops published. Step 3 (control): the same reserve at 20:00-22:00Z, outside BOTH windows.
response: Step 2: 200 {"data":{"groupId":"GRP-SELF-01","status":"assigned","provider":{"id":"groom_ops",...},"mode":"automatic","occurrences":[{"start":"2026-09-10T15:00:00.000Z","end":"2026-09-10T17:00:00.000Z","occurrenceNumber":1}],...}}. Step 3 control: 409 {"error":"NO_SCHEDULE_AVAILABLE","evaluations":[{"providerId":"groom_ops","eligible":false,"reasons":["Requested time is outside roster on 2026-09-10"]}]} - the roster gate is genuinely enforced, so the 15:00 success came from the fabricated window and not from a missing check.
d1_before: scheduling_availability: exactly one row [{id:'availability_groom_ops_2026-09-10_chennai-core', provider_id:'groom_ops', date:'2026-09-10', windows_json:'["09:00-10:00"]', source:'operations'}]. scheduling_reservations: empty. security_audit_events: one provider.availability.set by ops-scheduler@pawspace.test.
d1_after: scheduling_availability now holds a SECOND row written by the customer's request: {id:'uat_groom_ops_2026-09-10_chennai-core', provider_id:'groom_ops', date:'2026-09-10', windows_json:'["09:00-19:00"]', source:'uat_roster'}. Grouped counts: source 'operations' 1 row (2026-09-10 only), source 'uat_roster' 3 rows spanning 2026-09-10..2026-09-12 - the customer's single request minted forward-dated roster coverage for the provider on days Ops never published at all. scheduling_reservations: [{id:'GRP-SELF-01_groom_ops_1_...', customer_id:'CUST-SELF-01', provider_id:'groom_ops', scheduled_start:'2026-09-10T15:00:00.000Z', scheduled_end:'2026-09-10T17:00:00.000Z', status:'assigned'}]. No security_audit_events row exists for the roster rows the customer created - only the Ops set_availability is audited.
canonical_failure: POST /api/uat-scheduling calls seedUatRoster() on the customer's own reserve path (app/api/uat-scheduling/route.ts:24, invoked at line 67 after requireCustomerOwnership), which INSERTs scheduling_availability rows with a hard-coded per-service window and id 'uat_<providerId>_<date>_<zoneId>' for every governed provider in the requested city/zone - a distinct primary key from the Ops row 'availability_<providerId>_<date>_<zoneId>' - and repository.listAvailability() reads every row for that provider/date, so the customer's fabricated 09:00-19:00 window is unioned with and effectively overrides the narrower window Ops published under scheduling.manage.
blast_radius: Any holder of the customer role can, as a side effect of a normal booking attempt, write roster data for providers they have no authority over and book slots Operations deliberately closed - honouring a reduced-hours arrangement, a partial-day return from leave, or a capacity ramp becomes impossible because a customer request silently re-opens 09:00-19:00 (00:00-23:59 for boarding/overnight, 06:00-22:00 for pet_taxi, 06:00-21:00 for dog_walking). The fabrication also spans forward dates (100 days for dog_training/dog_walking; 3 days observed for grooming), so one request can re-open a provider's calendar well beyond the requested day, and none of these writes are recorded in security_audit_events, so Ops cannot see who reopened the window. Ops's own row is not deleted, so the divergence is invisible in the capacity-control read, which still shows the narrow 'operations' window.
